title: A bare https token stays in the backup when the URL does not start at the scheme
description: credentials() takes the scheme as every character before the first ://. A leading space or a leading newline makes that text fail the case-insensitive http and https checks. A userinfo with no colon then returns None. without_credentials returns None, and sanitized_config rewrites a backup url only when that call returns Some, so the token remains in the document. run() uses that document as the config payload. backup_to_git writes it to machines/<id>/config.toml and git push publishes the commit. shown_location uses the same None and prints the token. redacted() still masks it, because its scan keeps only the trailing scheme characters and calls shown_location on that slice. The clean URL https://dummy-token@example.test/repo.git becomes https://example.test/repo.git and is shown as https://***@example.test/repo.git.
root_cause: credentials() classifies the scheme with split_once on :// and treats a colon-free userinfo as a secret only when that whole prefix is http or https, ignoring ASCII case. A space or a newline before the scheme fails the test, so the function returns None. without_credentials and shown_location honor that None. sanitized_config leaves the url in place, and that is the config text backup_to_git writes and pushes.
intended_behavior: A bare http or https user name is removed, because it is often a token. The pushed config.toml has credentials removed from backup URLs. Commands print those credentials as ***.

trace.description: backup_add calls absolute_path and, when that returns None, keeps the caller's location string and passes it to add_target.
absolute_path returns None unless the argument is an existing directory. A git URL is not a directory, so a leading space or newline stays in the string.
add_target_locked stores that string with toml_edit::value in the new backup table's url field.
run reads config.toml and uses sanitized_config of that file as the single config payload for every target.
sanitized_config calls without_credentials on each backup url string and replaces the value only when the result is Some.
The scheme is the raw text before ://. Line 1144 accepts only http or https. Line 1146 returns None when the userinfo has no colon and that test failed, so dummy-token is not treated as a secret.
without_credentials returns None when credentials returns None. The rewrite at line 1060 does not run, so the original url remains in the document returned at line 1069.
backup_to_git writes those config bytes to machines/<id>/config.toml at line 1197, stages the file, and git push publishes the commit. A reader of the backup repository receives the bare token.

evidence.description: The scheme is url.split_once("://"), the whole prefix, not the trailing scheme token.
http is true only when that prefix equals http or https, ignoring ASCII case. A leading space or newline makes the comparison fail.
None if !http returns None. A colon-free userinfo is dropped only after the scheme test passes.
A userinfo that contains a colon still returns Some when the scheme test fails, and without_credentials keeps the user name. The confirmed case is the colon-free userinfo.
without_credentials returns None through credentials(). Line 1060 then leaves the toml url unchanged.

shown_location returns the original string when credentials returns None, so the bare token is printed. location_text at src/cli/backup.rs:175 and the list line at src/cli/backup.rs:607 go through shown_location.
redacted() walks backward only over ASCII scheme characters, then calls shown_location on that slice. A space or newline before https stays outside the slice, and the https slice is masked.
The without_credentials comment says a bare http(s) user name is often a token and is removed.
credentials_in_backup_urls_are_never_pushed expects https://TOKEN@github.com/a.git to become https://github.com/a.git.
parse_target keeps a non-empty url and does not trim it, so a leading space or newline remains on the stored location.
backup_add keeps the caller string when absolute_path returns None.
absolute_path returns None when the argument is not an existing directory.
On a config payload, backup_to_git writes those bytes to machines/<id>/config.toml before the push at line 1244.

The credentials section says backups never push the token and that the pushed config.toml has it removed. Line 247 says credentials are removed from backup URLs. Line 276 says every command prints credentials as ***.

conditions.description: The url string does not begin at the scheme, and its userinfo has no colon. The rerun used one leading space and one leading newline before https://dummy-token@example.test/repo.git.
The operator stores that string as a backup url. tsk backup add keeps a non-directory argument as written, and a quoted config.toml value keeps the same characters for sanitized_config.
A later backup run pushes the one sanitized config.toml. That document is the payload for every target, so a reachable target publishes the prefixed url. This rerun did not push.

execution.attacker_perspective: The lower-trust reader is anyone who can read the backup repository. The local operator supplied the url. The reader would see the bare token in the pushed machines/<id>/config.toml. This run compared the three strings inside a network namespace and did not contact a git remote.
instructions: The existing binary at /home/ubuntu/security-audit-skill/smarzban-tsk/run-2/agents/verifier-backup/scratch/check was executed and was not compiled in this run. Its source, check.rs, copies without_credentials, shown_location, redacted, and credentials from src/backup.rs.

The command was unshare --user --map-root-user --net --fork --pid --mount-proc env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=/home/ubuntu/security-audit-skill/smarzban-tsk/run-2/agents/verifier-backup/scratch TMPDIR=/home/ubuntu/security-audit-skill/smarzban-tsk/run-2/agents/verifier-backup/scratch timeout 10 /home/ubuntu/security-audit-skill/smarzban-tsk/run-2/agents/verifier-backup/scratch/check.

The program printed the Debug form of without_credentials, shown_location, and redacted for the clean URL, the leading-space URL, and the leading-newline URL. The new network namespace has no external route. Exit code was 0. No git remote was contacted and no push was performed.

remediation.strategy: Classify http(s) from the trailing scheme token the way redacted() already scans, and add a regression test that a leading space or newline before a bare https userinfo is removed by sanitized_config and masked by shown_location.

likelihood.reason: The URL must not start at the scheme. The clean https URL is stripped and masked. dummy-token remains only when a prefix such as a space or a newline sits before https:// and the userinfo has no colon.

impact.reason: A token the product promised to strip is written into the backup repository. The credentials section says the pushed config.toml has the token removed, and the code comment says a bare http(s) user name is removed too.

confidence.reason: Source and the rerun agree. The clean URL loses dummy-token. The leading-space and leading-newline URLs return without=None, and shown still contains dummy-token, while redacted masks both.

title: Windows state files inherit the parent directory DACL
description: At b5b92d60 the lower-trust reader is a second local Windows account that is not the file owner and is not an Administrator or SYSTEM. Those two principals are comparable to root, which can already read the Unix 0600 files. On Unix, tsk forces the state directory to 0700 and task files such as tsk.json to 0600 so another local user cannot read task data. On Windows, ensure_private_dir, create_private_file, and tighten_file set no security descriptor and no mode: a missing state directory is created with create_dir_all, and tsk.json is opened with OpenOptions that apply mode 0600 only under cfg(unix). tighten_file is a no-op off Unix, including on later load, so this repository never narrows a Windows DACL after creation. The header comment that no permission is claimed off Unix does not show whether the inherited parent DACL already excludes that second account. The installer creates the program directory and does not ACL the state directory. A second non-admin local account might read %LOCALAPPDATA%\tsk\tsk.json if that inherited DACL allows it. Source cannot show the inherited DACL.
claimed_root_cause: ensure_private_dir, create_private_file, and tighten_file apply owner-only mode bits only on Unix. On Windows they create the state directory and task files through std::fs with no security descriptor and never call a DACL API, so the directory and tsk.json keep the parent directory's inherited DACL and are not tightened later.

trace.description: When TSK_STATE_DIR is unset and LOCALAPPDATA is non-empty, the Windows default is that directory joined with tsk. Lines 1401-1403 return PathBuf::from(local).join("tsk"). Lines 1406-1409 fall back to USERPROFILE joined with .tsk when LOCALAPPDATA is empty.
Each supported save calls ensure_private_dir on the state directory at line 793, then tighten_state_files at line 795, before replacing tsk.json.
A missing directory is created with fs::create_dir_all. The Windows-only extra step is reject_reparse_ancestors at lines 35-36. tighten_private_dir, which applies 0700, is cfg(unix) at lines 55-56.

Each existing private state name, including tsk.json, is passed to tighten_file at line 1156. Load at line 714 and save at line 795 both call this function, so a later load is the same no-op off Unix.
The cfg(not(unix)) body at lines 300-303 discards the path. No mode bits and no security descriptor are written.

The temp document is opened with filesystem.create_file. StdFilesystem::create_file at line 283 calls create_private_file. tighten_state_files has already returned at line 795 and does not run again after this create.
OpenOptions is write, create, and truncate at line 175, then open. mode(0o600) exists only inside cfg(unix) at lines 176-179. The Windows open passes no security descriptor.

evidence.description: The module header says Unix state directories are 0700 and files are 0600, and that no permission is claimed on other platforms, where these helpers compile down to plain create and copy.
Before create_dir_all, Windows only calls reject_reparse_ancestors. The directory create attaches no security descriptor.
The directory tighten call is gated by cfg(unix); the Windows function returns after the reparse and directory checks.
options.mode(0o600) is inside the cfg(unix) block that begins at line 176.
Under cfg(not(unix)), tighten_file ignores its path. An existing Windows state file is not given an owner-only DACL.
The production AtomicFilesystem create_file implementation is create_private_file, with no Windows security-attribute argument.
Load calls tighten_state_files, which is a no-op off Unix.
The non-empty LOCALAPPDATA branch returns PathBuf::from(local).join("tsk").
When LOCALAPPDATA is unavailable, the Windows fallback returns PathBuf::from(userprofile).join(".tsk").
The storage guide documents the Windows default as LOCALAPPDATA\tsk, or USERPROFILE\.tsk when LOCALAPPDATA is unavailable, and does not document a Windows ACL.

blockers: The inherited DACL is an operating-system fact. This repository never sets or records a Windows security descriptor, so source cannot show whether a second non-admin account has an allow ACE.
This host is Linux and cannot create a Windows profile or query a DACL. That missing observation decides whether the inherited ACL is wider than the Unix owner-only control, and it was not performed.

validation_plan.local: On a fresh Windows 10 or 11 profile that is not a member of Administrators and is not elevated, leave TSK_STATE_DIR unset and do not pass --state-dir. Run tsk add with a dummy title so the default state directory and tsk.json are created. As that same user, run icacls with only the path, and no /grant, /deny, /remove, /reset, /setowner, /inheritance, /restore, or /replace, on %LOCALAPPDATA%\tsk and on %LOCALAPPDATA%\tsk\tsk.json and record every ACE and inheritance flag. If LOCALAPPDATA was unset, use %USERPROFILE%\.tsk instead. From a second local account that is also not a member of Administrators, attempt only to read those two paths and stop at access denied or at seeing the dummy text. Do not take ownership, change the ACL, or use an elevated token. If that second account can read the dummy text, the boundary the Unix build enforces with 0700 and 0600 is crossed. If access is denied and the DACL allows only the creating user, SYSTEM, and Administrators, the inherited DACL already matches that account boundary.
validation_plan.deployment: On an existing Windows store, run icacls with only the path on the state directory and on tsk.json. Do not change the ACL, do not take ownership, and do not open the task file. Record whether any allow ACE, including an inherited ACE, grants read to a principal other than the owner, SYSTEM, and Administrators. Stop after recording the DACL.
